name: RoboTwin 2.0
ability_definition: The ability to quickly move your hand, your hand together with your arm, or your two hands to grasp, manipulate, or assemble objects.

task_realism.reasoning: The 50 bimanual tabletop tasks involve recognizable workplace-adjacent actions: picking and placing diverse objects, handovers, stacking, opening containers, pressing and hanging items. They resemble simplified packing, handling and sorting work. However, they are mostly short-horizon pick-and-place with parallel-jaw grippers. They include little true assembly, fastening or fine finger manipulation, which is where much real manual dexterity is exercised.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Domain randomization (clutter, lighting, textures, table height) adds real-world-like variation. But evaluation is entirely in simulation, with simplified contact physics and no sensor noise from real hardware. Scoring is success rate only, with no time pressure or speed measurement, even though speed is central to the O*NET definition. The multi-task protocol also trains on randomized demos drawn from the same distribution as the test scenes, which narrows the generalization gap relative to real deployment.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It covers grasping and manipulation with one arm and with two coordinated arms across many object types, which matches the 'two hands' and 'hand with arm' parts of the definition. It omits the speed dimension, precise assembly, and in-hand dexterous manipulation with multi-fingered hands. It therefore measures a meaningful but partial slice of the ability.

format_match.reasoning: Inputs (multi-view camera images plus language instructions) and outputs (continuous arm and gripper action trajectories) mirror real robot control pipelines rather than artificial formats like multiple choice. Objects are realistic meshes. However, the artifacts are simulated scenes and binary task-success checks, not physical workpieces with quality or tolerance requirements.

transferability_reasoning: RoboTwin 2.0 tests genuine closed-loop bimanual manipulation across diverse objects and randomized scenes, so it captures the grasp-and-manipulate core of manual dexterity in a realistic control format. Transfer to real workplace dexterity is limited by simulation-only physics, simple grippers, sparse assembly content, and the absence of any speed metric. The multi-task protocol's in-distribution randomized training data further inflates scores relative to real-world generalization.

2025.metric: average success rate (%) over the 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, randomized setting
2025.human_reference: General adult workforce performing everyday two-handed manual handling (e.g., warehouse, assembly-line, or service workers)
